scope: Actual M capacity labels on all fourteen tools plus WAV alias at four widths; one genuine PNG compressed and downloaded, then a genuine 100 KB target run. Real resulting states are resized for four-width review. This is not a replacement for full tool regression or physical-device testing.

article.text: An upload form may use decimal KB or binary KiB. FileCompresser displays file sizes and targets in decimal units: 100 KB is 100,000 bytes and 1 MB is 1,000,000 bytes. Input, queue and extraction limits use MiB: 1 MiB is 1,048,576 bytes. Check the form’s written rule and inspect the downloaded file’s actual byte count. A target is a maximum, so a valid 92,000-byte output meets a 100,000-byte limit without being padded to match it.

publicationQualification: The stated size/capacity assertions passed; separate human review found an open-dialog resize/focus gap, with its own exact regression evidence. These results are not an overall UI/release acceptance. Oversized element screenshots can include the page’s sticky header at the current capture position; focus defect proof uses whole native viewport screenshots.
